title: Security Evidence Guide
readerIntent: Assemble reviewable evidence that the implemented Nodics deployment enforces its security claims.
priorKnowledge: Understand the identity-security journey and deployment architecture.
owner: Capability teams and deployment operators; evidence does not replace target-module authority
summary: Security evidence connects requirements to configuration, code contracts, tests, deployment state, monitoring, recovery, approvals, and known limitations without exposing secrets or sensitive data.

sections.heading: Evidence package
items: Scope: deployment, version, environment class, modules, topology, tenants, data classifications, providers, clients, trust boundaries, and exclusions.
Control map: requirement, threat, owner, authoritative configuration/source contract, test, runtime signal, recovery procedure, and approval.

Configuration proof: redacted effective security settings, exposure, origins, cookie policy, token lifetimes/audiences, permissions, provider capabilities, local-fallback state, and compatibility exceptions.
Test proof: exact commands, versions, environment assumptions, results, timestamps, negative/boundary cases, live-provider qualification, and unresolved limitations.
Operational proof: dashboards, alerts, safe audit samples, access reviews, credential rotation, backups/restores, incident exercises, capacity/load evidence, and change approvals.

sections.heading: Minimum identity and API cases
items: Valid login/access plus wrong password, inactive/locked principal, missing identity, expired/invalid token, audience/token-class mismatch, and revoked/security-stamp mismatch.
Missing permission, inherited permission, ownership, field masking, wrong tenant/enterprise, cross-tenant service-token denial, and service-only route rejection of human credentials.
Refresh rotation, replay, concurrent consume, CSRF/origin failure, logout, distributed invalidation, and strict-cache outage.
Unknown/disabled route exposure, invalid inputs and limits, safe status/error response, rate/abuse behavior, audit redaction, and dependency failure.

sections.heading: Evidence integrity
items: Never capture passwords, API keys, bearer/refresh tokens, private keys, full cookies, secret values, sensitive payloads, local absolute paths, or unrestricted stack/provider output.
Use correlation identifiers, safe reason codes, hashes or version identifiers, approved projections, access-controlled storage, retention, and tamper-evident audit where required.
Separate developer assertions from independently reviewed deployment evidence.
Record untested production dependencies and failed/waived controls explicitly; absence of evidence is not a pass.

sections.heading: Release decision
items: Confirm positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, distributed-race, security, performance, outage, recovery, upgrade, and regression evidence.
Require owners to accept residual risk and expiry dates for temporary exceptions.
Block release when required secrets, atomic shared state, tenant context, permissions, provider qualification, rollback, or monitoring cannot be trusted.
